title: Laser Grid
summary: Aim laser beams in 3D: set direction cosines, make beams perpendicular or at a given angle, and set the clearance between skew beams.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 11.2, Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line
learningOutcome: The student can turn direction ratios into direction cosines, find an unknown ratio for perpendicular lines or a given angle, and find the shortest distance between two skew lines.

levels.title: Aim the beam
levels.adds: Baseline: direction cosines are the direction ratios divided by √(a² + b² + c²), and l² + m² + n² = 1 (Ex 11.1 Q3, Q5; Examples 2, 3).
hints: Find the length of the target’s position: √(x² + y² + z²).
Divide each coordinate by that length to get a cosine.
Multiply each cosine by the denominator shown to get the numerators.

levels.title: Right angle
levels.adds: New: two lines are perpendicular when a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ = 0, which gives the unknown ratio (Ex 11.2 Q10, Q11; Misc Q3; Example 8).
hints: Write the dot product of the two sets of ratios with p in it.
Set the dot product equal to 0.
Solve the one equation for p.

levels.title: A set angle
levels.adds: New: cos θ = (a·b)/(|a||b|); an unknown ratio changes |b| as well, so test whole-number values (Ex 11.2 Q8, Q9; Examples 7, 8).
hints: Write a·b and |b| with the unknown c in them.
Try whole values of c that make |b| a whole number.
Compare the cosine with the fraction wanted.

levels.title: Skew clearance
levels.adds: New: the distance between skew lines is |(a₂ − a₁)·(b₁ × b₂)|/|b₁ × b₂| (Ex 11.2 Q12 to Q15; Example 9).
hints: Find b₁ × b₂ and its length first.
Dot the offset (with h in it) with b₁ × b₂.
Divide by |b₁ × b₂| and match the distance wanted.

misconceptions: Direction ratios are the same as direction cosines
Lines that never meet are always parallel
The angle between two lines depends on where they pass
